name: Ben Allen
title: California State Senator, Chair of the Senate Energy, Utilities and Communications Committee
district: California State Senate District 24 (Westside and South Bay Los Angeles County, Hollywood, Santa Monica Mountains; represented as District 26 from 2014 to 2022 before redistricting)
years_of_service: December 1, 2014 to present. Allen is term-limited; his current term ends December 7, 2026, and he is not seeking re-election to the Senate. He placed second in the June 2, 2026 top-two primary for California Insurance Commissioner (behind Jane Kim) and is a candidate for that office in the November 2026 general election.
background: Allen grew up in what is now his Senate district; his father taught English at UCLA and his mother was a public-school teacher and artist who chaired the Santa Monica Arts Commission. He graduated from Santa Monica High School in 1996, earned a B.A. magna cum laude in History from Harvard University in 2000, an M.Phil. in Latin American Studies from the University of Cambridge in 2001, and a J.D. from UC Berkeley in 2008. He is fluent in Spanish. (Source: official Senate biography, sd24.senate.ca.gov/biography.)

Before the Senate, Allen worked as Communications Director for U.S. Rep. José Serrano (D-NY), as a Washington staffer for the National Democratic Institute's Latin America team, and as an attorney at Bryan Cave LLP, Richardson & Patel, and the nonprofit Spark Program. He lectured at UCLA Law School and, as President of the Santa Monica-Malibu Unified School District Board of Education, led the local school board before running for the Legislature. (Source: official Senate biography.)

Allen was elected to the State Senate in November 2014, defeating fellow Democrat Sandra Fluke 60.3% to 39.7% in the general election for the open District 26 seat. He was re-elected in 2018 with 77.2% of the vote against Baron Bruno, and in 2022, after redistricting moved his seat to District 24, with 67.1% against Republican Kristina Irwin. He has chaired the Senate Education Committee in earlier sessions and currently chairs the Senate Energy, Utilities and Communications Committee. (Source: Ballotpedia, Ben Allen.)

voting_record_highlights: SB 277 (2015 to 2016), eliminating the personal-belief exemption from school vaccination requirements: Allen was a lead author with Sen. Richard Pan. It passed the Senate concurrence vote 24 to 14 on June 29, 2015, and was signed by Gov. Jerry Brown on June 30, 2015 as Chapter 35, Statutes of 2015. (Source: leginfo.legislature.ca.gov bill status for SB 277.)

SB 450 (2015 to 2016), the Voter's Choice Act, authorizing counties to conduct elections by mailing ballots to all voters combined with vote centers: Allen was a lead author with Sen. Bob Hertzberg. It passed the Senate concurrence vote 27 to 11 on August 29, 2016, and was signed September 29, 2016 as Chapter 832, Statutes of 2016. (Source: leginfo.legislature.ca.gov bill status for SB 450.)

SB 54 (2021 to 2022), the California Plastic Pollution Prevention and Packaging Producer Responsibility Act: Allen was one of six co-lead authors (with Hertzberg, Luz Rivas, Skinner, Stern, and Wiener). It passed the Senate concurrence vote 29 to 0 on June 30, 2022, and was signed the same day as Chapter 75, Statutes of 2022. (Source: leginfo.legislature.ca.gov bill status for SB 54.)

SB 42 (2025 to 2026), the California Fair Elections Act of 2026: Allen was one of three lead Senate authors (with Umberg and Cervantes). The Senate concurred in Assembly amendments 29 to 8 on September 13, 2025, and Gov. Gavin Newsom signed it October 2, 2025 as Chapter 245, Statutes of 2025, placing the measure before voters as Proposition 4 on the November 2026 ballot. Full detail on the measure itself is covered in content/measures/ca-prop-4-2026.json and is not duplicated here. (Source: leginfo.legislature.ca.gov bill status for SB 42.)
attendance: No individually published floor-attendance or voting-participation record for Senator Allen was found. The California State Senate does not publish a per-member attendance scorecard; the only public records are bill-by-bill roll-call votes at leginfo.legislature.ca.gov, which is what the voting-record entries above are drawn from. A third-party tool, CalMatters' Digital Democracy (calmatters.digitaldemocracy.org/legislators/benjamin-allen-70), tracks his bill-passage counts and interest-group vote-alignment percentages but likewise does not publish an attendance metric.
